skills.title: Client email intake
skills.summary: Find the client and deal by the sender's email (on the CRM if your organisation has one, otherwise on Monday), save the attachments to the deal folder and register them on the deal.
skills.details: For the email you choose, the assistant finds the client and deal on your organisation's CRM by the sender's email address (if the organisation has no CRM, it finds the Deal on Monday), finds the deal folder (the folder the CRM has linked or will link to the deal, usually under Customers/; if there is none, it creates one with a tmp/ folder), saves the attachments that aren't there yet into tmp/ to be checked later, then registers those files on the deal on the CRM. It reads the email from the mail account you added on this computer (Sign in with Microsoft or IMAP). Only if your organisation uses the enterprise shared-mailbox connection and this computer has no mail account does it read the email through the app's server instead, which copies the attachments straight into the deal's tmp/ on OneDrive, leaving out signature logos and pictures in the email body. If there is no client or deal yet, the assistant proposes creating them and only creates them when you agree. Asking it to process an email covers creating the folder, saving the files and registering them, in Ask first and Full access mode; in Plan only mode it only says what it would do. The assistant doesn't rename files, change Monday, reply to the email or mark it as read; files stay in tmp/ until they are checked and you approve filing.
examples: Process this email and save the files to the deal
Save the documents the client sent in this email to the deal

skills.title: Check loan documents
skills.summary: Check a client's documents against the 23-item checklist and report what needs doing; with the CRM, process a deal's new files from any source and file them when you approve.
skills.details: The assistant checks the source file (genuine issued copy, edited, photo or scan), recognises the document type, reads it by that type's rules and cross-checks the documents; the report gives the conclusion, Fact Find details and what to tell the client. With the CRM, when you ask it to process or check a deal it takes every new file in the deal's tmp/, from any source (client portal, email, your upload, files dropped into OneDrive), even before OneDrive syncs it to your computer: it registers each file on the deal with its type and client, links it to a required document, records the results and proposes filing. In Ask first mode it asks once before changing the CRM. It files, renames or accepts only when you agree and never copies TFNs, Medicare or card numbers.
examples: What's new for the Whitmore deal?
Has any client sent new documents?
Check the payslip and statement I just attached

skills.title: Australian business lookup (ABN)
skills.summary: Look up an ABN, ACN or business name: active or cancelled, GST, and whether it matches the name on the document.
skills.details: The assistant looks up the business on the Australian Business Register's ABN Lookup, gives the entity name, entity type, ABN status (active or cancelled, and since when), GST and business names, then lists what needs action: a cancelled ABN, a wrong ABN number, or a business name that differs from the document (allowing for trust names and sole traders' names). A printout or screenshot of an ABN Lookup result sent by the client is looked up again, not used as evidence. Registration status with ASIC (whether a company has been deregistered) isn't in the ABR, so the assistant says clearly that it couldn't check it. The assistant never guesses business details from memory.
examples: Is ABC Pty Ltd still active?
